## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `affa89e7a95770bce88e9ba76231028a75659834`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/README.md, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md + none
Security-touching: no

Read: card #36611 (body and its 4 comments), PR #36625 (body, 3 files, net diff against merge-base `ed0edb1b50`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `main` (`27895d7ff6`; no file under `skills/`, `packages/spec/src/ui`, `ui/packages/plugin-form`, `ui/packages/core/src/actions`, `FormPage.tsx` or `recordFormFields.ts` differs between the merge-base and `main`). Security line: the only security-adjacent words in a changed hunk are "public form", named as one reader of `sections`; no hunk teaches sharing, permission, credential, token or authentication behaviour.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. Three files, all prose: two skill passages and one changeset. No schema, no validator, no lint rule, no eval case, no generated output. Right.
- Public surface: the shipped text of `@objectstack/skills` changes in two passages. Right, and it is a correction toward `main`, not a new capability.
- `skills/README.md` "Screen flows vs. views" now names the door: a named form view of `type: 'wizard'` opened by an action of `type: 'form'`, and says an object's own New and Edit never step. Right (see ④).
- `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` sections bullet now says who reads `sections` and who does not, and drops the `pane` example. Right (see ④).
- Token ratchet: `navigation.md` is the one ratcheted file; the PR states 2554 before and after against a ceiling of 2564, with no ceiling edited (no ratchet file is in the diff). The verdict belongs to the lint lanes, see the check-run note below. `skills/README.md` grows by two lines and is stated to sit outside the ratchet population; not re-measured here.

Check-runs on the head at the time of reading (41 total): no run has failed. Concluded success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped Lint lanes, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, filter. Still in progress, so NO verdict yet: Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Build Core, Test Core (1/10) and (2/10). The skills lanes (token ratchet, skill links, skill docs) sit among the unfinished Lint lanes: this record's PASS is the contract judgment, and the adopting seat reads those conclusions on this head before it lands anything. The rest are skipped by path filter.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — agreed. The changeset `.changeset/36611-skills-wizard-routing-sections.md` bumps `@objectstack/skills` (`packages/skills/package.json`) at patch, the level every sibling skill-wording changeset on `main` uses, and it carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the PR body. The diff publishes corrected prose only: no key, value, default or refusal changes, and nothing an existing author wrote stops working. Patch is right. Check Changeset concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, out of scope 1: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:44` still reads "an **objectstack-ui** form view, `type: 'wizard'`" with no door named. Confirmed at the head. It does not contradict the README (it is the shorter form of the same routing), and the claim comment 7091050497 on the card puts that file in stage 2, Blocked-by #36158. Left to stage 2 of #36611; not a finding on this head.
- Dev flag, out of scope 2: an `object-form` page block also takes `formType: 'wizard'` (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:7220` on `main`), a second ui home the README bullet does not name. Answered in ④ as N1.
- Dev deviation 1 (a classifier refusal of an empty-branch push, then the ordinary task push continued): a process matter for the seat, outside the contract faces; it changes nothing in the reviewed tree. Escalated to the adopting seat as written, not judged here.
- Dev deviation 2 (intermediate head at 2564 tokens, final head back to 2554): only the final head is reviewed. No flag.
- Dev deviation 3 (two dist-reading gates not measured locally): CI decides; Build Core and the Type Check gates were still running at reading time (see ①).
- Card scope: stage 1 covers item 3's README half and item 4; items 1 and 2 and item 3's automation half stay open for stage 2, and the PR says `Part of #36611`, so the card stays open. The card asks for "the evals that exercise it": no eval file changes here. At the head, `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/triggers.json:48` already routes a three-step create wizard to the UI skill and `views-apps-actions-pages.json:186-190` already exercises "New and Edit are built from the object, no form view"; no existing case contradicts either new passage. Whether stage 2 owes a case for the named wizard form is stage 2's question.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No code, no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/README.md`, "Screen flows vs. views", against `main`:

- "a named form view (`type: 'wizard'`) that an action of `type: 'form'` opens": holds. `ActionType` lists `form` and its `target` is the FormView name (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:693`, `:719`); `ActionRunner.executeForm` navigates to `/forms/NAME` (`ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:2931-2939`); `FormPage` draws one step per section for `type: 'wizard'` (`ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx:2848`); the form view `type` enum is `simple | tabbed | wizard` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:5341-5343`).
- "An object's own New and Edit never step: they are built from its fields and `fieldGroups`": holds. The three console hosts take their field list from `recordFormFieldNames` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/recordFormFields.ts`, called at `AppContent.tsx:1791`, `RecordFormPage.tsx:296`, `useActionModal.tsx:289`), whose own header says no internal form view selects, orders or groups the list; `packages/lint/src/validate-internal-form-views.ts` warns `form-view-internal-not-loaded` for the inert forms.
- The screen-flow half is unchanged and agrees with the README's own skill table (line 51) and with `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:44`.
- Agreement inside the bundle: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` "Form Views" (lines 344-372 at the head) teaches exactly this door, so the index now routes to what the skill teaches.

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md`, "Record Presentation", sections bullet, against `main`:

- "New and Edit never read them": holds, same three hosts as above. The link `./list-views.md#form-views` resolves to the `## Form Views` heading at the head.
- "a named or public form ... do": holds. One `FormPage` serves both routes (`/forms/:name` and `/f/:slug`, `ui/apps/console/src/App.tsx:348` and the internal route) and reads `form.sections`, resolving `{ group }` through `resolveSectionGroupReferences` (`FormPage.tsx:845-857`).
- "a page's `record:details` or form block do": holds for exactly these page blocks. `record:details` takes `sections` with a `group` reference (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:1327`, `:1379`, `:1549`) and its renderer resolves it (`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx:897-925`); `object-form` and `object-master-detail-form` take `sections` (`component.zod.ts:7259`, `:7540`), resolved in `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/ObjectForm.tsx:336`. The record DETAIL page with no page authored is not a reader of form-view sections on `main` (`RecordDetailView.tsx` and `recordDetailSections.ts` read the object's field groups and no form view), and the sentence does not claim it is: it says "a page's `record:details` ... block", the authored block. `rules/record-page.md` step 1 keeps teaching the derived Details sections. No overclaim.
- Ladder step 2, "restating a group's key is refused": holds on every reader named (`sectionGroupReferenceRefinement` at `view.zod.ts:4686`, `component.zod.ts:1549` and `:7171`). Dropping "at parse" loses nothing an author acts on.
- Ladder step 3, "a wizard's steps" in place of "a wizard/pane structure": holds. `pane` left the form-view section in spec 18.3.0 (`view.zod.ts:4106-4118`, `FORM_SECTION_PANE_RETIRED`) and the page-block section too (`component.zod.ts:6556-6559`); `group` on a wizard step is refused (`view.zod.ts:5726-5737`), so a wizard step is the true case that must enumerate `fields`, and it agrees with "Form Views" ("each listing `fields`, never `{ group }`"). No other file under `skills/` points at a section `pane` (the remaining hits for the word are the gantt "left-pane" comment and unrelated prose).
- The cuts that pay for the new sentence ("in order", "when one surface needs a local arrangement", "at all", "genuinely", "at parse", "beside it", the shorter last sentence): each is emphasis or restatement. The three steps, their order, the group-reference example, the refusal, the named-customer condition, the comment requirement and the staleness warning all survive. No teaching is lost.

Tried to break it: an action descriptor that passes its own `fields` or `sections` to `useActionModal` skips the object-derived layout (`useActionModal.tsx:286`), but that is a code-level descriptor, not a form view and not the object's New or Edit, so the sentence stands. A wizard form with one section draws stacked (`FormPage.tsx:2848`), consistent with "a step per section". A `{ group }` section on a public form resolves the same as on a named form.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — `skills/README.md` names one ui home for a stepped single-object form, the named wizard form. An `object-form` page block with `formType: 'wizard'` is a second one on `main` (`component.zod.ts:7220`). The bullet routes to a skill and names the home that skill's "Form Views" teaches, so nothing taught is wrong. Left as an accepted deviation; stage 2 may add it if the automation line is rewritten to match.

N2 (nit) — `navigation.md` says "form block" without the block names (`object-form`, `object-master-detail-form`), which an author cannot search for. The token budget explains the brevity and `rules/list-views.md` "Master-Detail Forms" names the second block. Left as an accepted deviation.
